title: Compute total time to finish all courses (per-task duration)
description_html:
Given a list of courses, each with prerequisite dependencies and a required time. Courses can run in parallel (in batches). Compute the shortest total time to finish all courses, assuming there are no cyclic dependencies.

Input

  • A 2D array describing the schedule — each element gives a course's prerequisite dependencies (a batch of courses that must precede it).
  • A 1D array time[] giving each course's duration.

Output

The shortest time to complete all courses. A course may start only once all of its prerequisites have finished; courses with no pending prerequisites run concurrently. If the dependencies contain a cycle, completion is impossible.

Semantics of "batch" (clarify with the interviewer)

  • Per-course start (critical path) — each course begins the instant its own prerequisites finish. finish[v] = time[v] + max(finish[prereqs]); answer = max(finish). (Same as LC 2050 Parallel Courses III.)
  • Barrier batches — every course in the current batch must finish before the next batch starts. answer = Σ over batches of max(time in batch). (Same shape as LC 1136 Parallel Courses, weighted.)

Example (critical path)

prerequisites = [[1, 0]]   # course 1 depends on course 0
time          = [3, 2]     # course 0 takes 3, course 1 takes 2
result        = 5          # 0 finishes at t=3, then 1 finishes at 3+2 = 5

Cycle detection: run Kahn's algorithm — if fewer than n courses are dequeued, a cycle exists (impossible).
